items.description: Upper River Derwent, Stonethwaite Beck and Derwent Water
items.message:
Due to Derwent Water remaining high following recent rainfall a Flood Alert will remain in force.  Derwent Water level is currently receding and will continue to do so over the coming days as high pressure builds bringing a period of settled and dry weather.  
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near the Upper Derwent from Seathwaite to Derwent Water. 
We continue to closely monitor the situation. Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Friday 30 October or as the situation changes.

items.description: Tidal Thames riverside from Putney Bridge to Teddington Weir
items.eaAreaName: Kent, South London and East Sussex

floodArea.county: Greater London, Hammersmith and Fulham, Hounslow, Richmond upon Thames, Wandsworth

items.message:
High tides this afternoon may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 03:30 PM to 05:30 PM on Thursday 29th October.
River levels are expected to be high as a result of spring tides.

The next high tide at Richmond at 04:30 PM on 29/10/2026, may result in brief low-level flooding of riverside roads and open spaces.

Astronomical tide levels are falling. The river flow at Teddington Weir is 8 cubic metres per second and is steady. We anticipate the flows to remain low for the next few days.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 6:00PM on Thursday 29 October or as the situation changes.

items.description: The tidal River Waveney from Ellingham to Breydon Water
items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding.
Weather conditions are expected to improve and no further flooding is expected.

Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

items.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
items.message:
Higher than normal tides today may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from 12 noon to 3pm today, Thursday 29 October. 
We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak. The weather forecast is improving, and we expect levels to start returning to normal soon. We are monitoring rainfall and river levels. Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 10am on Friday 30 October  or as the situation changes.

floodArea.riverOrSea: River Brathay, River Rothay, River Winster

items.message:
Due to Windermere Lake remaining high following recent rainfall a Flood Alert will remain in force.  Windermere Lake level is currently receding and will continue to do so over the coming days as high pressure builds bringing a period of settled and dry weather.  
Locations most affected will be the rivers Brathay, Rothay, Winster and other watercourses from Grasmere to Grange-over-Sands, including low lying areas around Ambleside, Skelwith Bridge, Windermere, Hawkshead, Newby Bridge, Backbarrow, Cark and Cartmel. 
We continue to closely monitor the situation. Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Friday 30 October or as the situation changes.
